A severe form of leishmaniasis characterized by irregular bouts of fever, substantial weight loss, swelling of the spleen and liver, and anemia (which may be serious). Praziquantel is the only drug I found that fits both conditions. It has a Drugs@FDA generic (ANDA208820, tablet, prescription), and Open Targets lists it for schistosomiasis (schistosomiasis due to *S. haematobium*, *S. japonicum* and *S. mansoni*). Open Targets labels its status for the helminthiasis indication as Approved. The Phase 3 label shown on the card applies to cysticercosis.

Oxamniquine is also approved for schistosomiasis in Open Targets, but Drugs@FDA has no record of it, so it has no US generic.

I couldn't check mefloquine or artesunate. The CLI connection dropped on those lookups, and I never confirmed whether Open Targets lists either one for schistosomiasis. Both appeared in trials, so a missed match is possible. A drug search by indication also returned only praziquantel.
